_about: Field help for the config editor's Form view: what each key is and what changing it does. 'files' maps a system and file id (glob: * = any text) to the catalogs it uses, first listed wins on a tie. In a pattern, * = any one key, # = any list index, ** = any number of further levels. Text may use `code`. Where a system's behaviour is not documented, say less rather than guess.

schema_version.what: The version of the routes file format. Switchyard and the Relay plugin read version `1`.
schema_version.change: Any other value makes the whole file fail to load; leave it at 1.

llm_clients.*.what: An upstream connection: the address, wire format and credential that the targets naming this block use. Each target picks one with `llm_client`.

llm_clients.*.format.what: The API format spoken to this upstream: `openai_chat` (`/v1/chat/completions`), `openai_responses` or `anthropic_messages` (`/v1/messages`).
llm_clients.*.format.change: Requests to every target on this client are sent in the new format, so the upstream must serve it (LiteLLM serves `openai_chat` and `anthropic_messages`). The Relay plugin does not translate between formats: there, the client format must match what the calling agent speaks, or its requests fail.

llm_clients.*.base_url.what: Where requests for this client go: the upstream's base URL (http or https, loopback or an in-network service name such as `litellm`).
llm_clients.*.base_url.change: Every target on this client starts calling the new address. An address outside the lab is refused here: reaching it needs an egress-allowlist change, not a routes edit.

llm_clients.*.api_key_env.what: The NAME of the environment variable holding the key sent upstream. The file never holds the key itself. Cannot be combined with `forward_auth`.
llm_clients.*.api_key_env.change: The new variable must exist and be non-empty in Switchyard's (or the Relay gateway's) environment when it starts, or the file fails to load and calls through this client are refused.

llm_clients.*.forward_auth.what: true = pass each caller's own `Authorization` header upstream instead of a stored key (default false).
llm_clients.*.forward_auth.change: true: no key lives in Switchyard, and every caller must send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, which the router then checks. false: the client needs `api_key_env` and a key in the environment.

llm_clients.*.max_retries.what: How many times a failed upstream call is retried before the request fails (0–10, default 2).
llm_clients.*.max_retries.change: Higher rides over brief engine hiccups but makes real failures slower and repeats load on a struggling engine; 0 fails on the first error.

llm_clients.*.extra_headers.what: HTTP headers added to every request on this client.

llm_clients.*.extra_headers.*.what: One HTTP header added to every request on this client.
llm_clients.*.extra_headers.*.change: The upstream receives the new header value on every call. A header owned by the auth mode (such as Authorization) is refused.

llm_clients.*.timeout_ms.what: How long one upstream call may take, in milliseconds (unset = no limit).
llm_clients.*.timeout_ms.change: Lower fails slow calls sooner (long generations may be cut off); higher waits longer on a stuck engine.

targets.*.what: A target: one model reached through one llm client. Routes name targets, never models. Its identity is the pair (`id`, `llm_client`).

targets.*.id.what: The exact model name sent upstream: a router (LiteLLM) alias.
targets.*.id.change: Every route using this target is served by the new model. Two targets with the same (`id`, `llm_client`) pair are collapsed and one is dropped with only a warning, taking its `system_prompt` with it.

targets.*.llm_client.what: Which `[llm_clients.*]` block this target is reached through.
targets.*.llm_client.change: Changes the address, wire format and credential used for this target. It must name an existing client.

targets.*.system_prompt.what: A system prompt prepended whenever this target serves a completion.
targets.*.system_prompt.change: The steering changes for EVERY route that uses this target, including `direct-*` passthroughs. Judge (classifier) calls do not receive it.

targets.*.reasoning_effort.what: A reasoning effort forced on every request to this target, replacing the caller's value.
targets.*.reasoning_effort.change: Every request served by this target uses the new effort: higher thinks longer (slower, more tokens), lower answers faster.

targets.*.extra_body.what: Extra JSON fields merged into each upstream request body for this target, when the request does not already set them.

targets.*.extra_body.**.what: A request-body field sent upstream for this target (for example `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`), unless the caller sets it.
targets.*.extra_body.**.change: The engine receives the new value on every request through this target.

routes.*.what: A route: a model name clients can call. Its `type` decides how each request picks a target.

routes.*.id.what: The public model name clients send to use this route (for example `auto-local`). Keep it equal to the block's key.
routes.*.id.change: Clients still calling the old name stop matching this route: Switchyard answers unknown model, and Relay passes the name through unrouted. Every client config that names the route must change too.

routes.*.type.what: How the route chooses a target: `passthrough` (always one target), `stage_router` (starts on one tier, escalates on tool-activity signals), `llm_classifier` (a judge model grades the request), `random`, `noop`, `auto` and others.
routes.*.type.change: Each type takes a different set of keys; switching type means rewriting the route's other fields, and keys that do not belong to the new type are refused at load.

routes.*.target.what: passthrough: the one target this route always uses.
routes.*.target.change: All calls to this route go to the new target's model.

routes.*.context_window.what: The context window advertised for this route in `/v1/models` (Relay also exports it to Claude Code). It does not enforce a limit.
routes.*.context_window.change: Clients plan their prompts against the new number. Keep it the SMALLEST window among the targets that can serve the route: if it is larger, long prompts fail on the smaller engine (often before they can escalate).

routes.*.tool_calling.what: Whether the route accepts tool calls. false = tool definitions and tool history are refused with HTTP 400; true or unset = no restriction.
routes.*.tool_calling.change: false breaks every agent that sends tools to this route; true only advertises the capability.

routes.*.reasoning.what: Whether the route accepts reasoning controls. false = reasoning parameters are refused with HTTP 400.
routes.*.reasoning.change: false makes requests that set a reasoning effort fail on this route.

routes.*.vision.what: Whether the route accepts images. false = image inputs are refused with HTTP 400; also shown as `capabilities.vision` in `/v1/models`.
routes.*.vision.change: true advertises image support: only set it when every target of the route accepts images.

routes.*.capable_target.what: stage_router: the stronger (slower, costlier) tier that takes escalated turns.
routes.*.capable_target.change: Escalated turns go to the new target. Its window must be at least the route's `context_window`.

routes.*.efficient_target.what: stage_router: the fast tier. With `picker = efficient_first` it answers every turn that is not escalated.
routes.*.efficient_target.change: Most traffic on the route moves to the new target. Keep the route's `context_window` no larger than its window.

routes.*.picker.what: stage_router: the default tier. `efficient_first` starts on the efficient tier and escalates only when signals (or the classifier) clearly say so; `capable_first` (experimental) does the reverse.
routes.*.picker.change: Swapping it flips which tier serves the undecided turns, so cost, latency and answer quality all move.

routes.*.confidence_threshold.what: stage_router: the width of the 'undecided' band (0–1) on the tool-signal score. Turns with a score outside the band are decided by the signals; turns inside it go to the classifier, then to the picker's default tier.
routes.*.confidence_threshold.change: Raising it sends more turns to the classifier and the default tier (with `efficient_first`: fewer escalations); lowering it lets the tool signals decide more turns. Without a `classifier` block nothing escalates whatever this is.

routes.*.recent_turn_window.what: stage_router: how many of the latest tool results the escalation signals look at (default 3).
routes.*.recent_turn_window.change: Larger reacts to a longer history of tool failures and successes; smaller reacts only to the latest ones.

routes.*.capable_hold_turns.what: stage_router: how many requests stay on the capable tier after an escalation (default 2; 0 = none, -1 = for the rest of the session).
routes.*.capable_hold_turns.change: Higher keeps a hard task on the strong model longer (more cost); lower drops back to the efficient tier sooner.

routes.*.handoff_notes.what: Notes added to the conversation when the route switches tier.

routes.*.handoff_notes.escalation_note.what: Text appended when a turn escalates to the capable tier, so that model knows it is continuing another model's work.
routes.*.handoff_notes.escalation_note.change: The capable model reads the new wording on every escalation; without a note it tends to redo work the efficient tier already did.

routes.*.handoff_notes.deescalation_note.what: Text appended when the route drops back to the efficient tier.
routes.*.handoff_notes.deescalation_note.change: The efficient model reads the new wording whenever it takes over again.

routes.*.classifier.what: stage_router: the judge that decides the undecided turns. WITHOUT THIS BLOCK THE ROUTE NEVER ESCALATES: every turn reports confidence 0 and falls through to the default tier.

routes.*.classifier.target.what: The judge: the target asked to grade each undecided turn. It is not a routing destination.
routes.*.classifier.target.change: The new model grades the turns. A reasoning model that spends its budget thinking returns empty verdicts; a fast model with thinking off is the safe choice.

routes.*.classifier.base_threshold.what: The lowest judged probability that the efficient tier can solve the turn (`p_solve`, 0–1) that still keeps it on the efficient tier; below it the turn escalates.
routes.*.classifier.base_threshold.change: Raising it escalates more turns to the capable tier (better answers, more cost and latency); lowering it keeps more on the efficient tier.

routes.*.classifier.threshold_step.what: Added to `base_threshold` for uncertain or unmatched verdicts (twice for unsupported ones).
routes.*.classifier.threshold_step.change: Raising it sends doubtful turns to the capable tier more readily.

routes.*.classifier.max_output_tokens.what: The token budget for the judge's verdict (default 4096).
routes.*.classifier.max_output_tokens.change: Too small and a judge that thinks before answering returns nothing usable, so the turn takes the fallback; larger costs more judge time per turn.

routes.*.classifier.classify_trigger.what: When the judge runs: `every_request`, or (on builds that accept it) `new_session` to judge once per conversation.
routes.*.classifier.classify_trigger.change: `new_session` cuts judge calls to one per conversation, at the price of keeping the first decision for the whole session.

routes.*.mode.what: llm_classifier: what the judge decides. `capability` = can the weak model solve this (`p_solve`); also `escalation`, `custom`, `direct`.
routes.*.mode.change: Each mode takes different keys; changing it usually means rewriting the route.

routes.*.classifier_target.what: llm_classifier: the judge target that grades each request. It is not a routing destination.
routes.*.classifier_target.change: The new model grades requests; if it fails or returns an unusable verdict, the request goes to `strong_target`.

routes.*.strong_target.what: llm_classifier: the capable tier, used when the judge says the weak model is unlikely to solve the request, and on any judge failure.
routes.*.strong_target.change: Hard requests (and every judge failure) go to the new target.

routes.*.weak_target.what: llm_classifier: the fast tier, used when the judged `p_solve` is at least the threshold.
routes.*.weak_target.change: Requests judged easy go to the new target.

routes.*.base_threshold.what: llm_classifier: the lowest judged solve probability (`p_solve`, 0–1) that routes to `weak_target`.
routes.*.base_threshold.change: Raising it sends more traffic to `strong_target` (better answers, more cost and latency); lowering it sends more to `weak_target`. `base_threshold + 2 x threshold_step` must stay at most 1.

routes.*.threshold_step.what: llm_classifier: added to the threshold once for uncertain verdicts and twice for unsupported ones (default 0).
routes.*.threshold_step.change: Raising it sends doubtful requests to `strong_target` more readily.

routes.*.classify_trigger.what: llm_classifier: when the judge runs. `every_request` (default, including tool continuations), `user_turn` (each new user message), `new_session` (once per conversation, then the target is kept).
routes.*.classify_trigger.change: Fewer judge calls mean less latency and judge load, but an early decision is kept for longer.

routes.*.message_hash_fallback.what: llm_classifier: when the client sends no session id, key the session on a hash of the first user message (needs `classify_trigger` `new_session` or `user_turn`).
routes.*.message_hash_fallback.change: true lets clients without session headers be judged once per conversation; false judges them again on every request.

routes.*.fail_open.what: What happens when the judge fails or times out.
routes.*.fail_open.change: Changes whether a broken judge falls back to the default tier or fails the request.

routes.*.max_output_tokens.what: llm_classifier: the token budget for the judge's verdict (default 4096).
routes.*.max_output_tokens.change: Too small and a thinking judge returns nothing usable (the request then goes to `strong_target`).

llm_clients.what: The upstream connections, one block per client.

targets.what: The targets (model + client pairs) routes can use, one block per target.

routes.what: The routes (callable model names), one block per route. At least one is required.

version.what: The version of the plugins file format.
version.change: Another value makes Relay refuse the file.

plugins.what: The plugins Relay loads and the policy their signatures must meet.

plugins.dynamic.#.what: One native plugin Relay loads at start (here: the Switchyard routing plugin).

plugins.dynamic.#.manifest.what: Path to the plugin's manifest, which names its library file and checksum.
plugins.dynamic.#.manifest.change: Relay loads a different plugin build at the next gateway start; it must pass the signature policy below.

plugins.dynamic.#.config.priority.what: The plugin's place in Relay's processing order: plugins with a lower number run first.
plugins.dynamic.#.config.priority.change: Moves routing before or after the other components (for example PII redaction), which changes what each one sees.

plugins.dynamic.#.config.switchyard_conf.what: The routes file the Switchyard plugin reads (`clients/nemo-relay/routes.toml`).
plugins.dynamic.#.config.switchyard_conf.change: The gateway routes with the other file after its next restart.

plugins.policy.defaults.attestation.what: How strictly plugin signatures are checked. `signature` requires a valid signature from a trusted key; `integrity_only` checks only the checksum.
plugins.policy.defaults.attestation.change: `integrity_only` would let anyone who can write the plugin directory replace the library and its checksum together. Security policy: edit it on the host, not here.

plugins.policy.defaults.trusted_public_k.what: A public key whose plugin signatures Relay trusts.
plugins.policy.defaults.trusted_public_k.change: Adding a key trusts every plugin it signs; removing the key that signed the installed plugin stops Relay from loading it.

components.#.what: A built-in Relay component and its settings.

components.#.kind.what: Which component this block configures, for example `pii_redaction` or `observability`.
components.#.kind.change: Changing it makes Relay read this block's config as a different component; usually wrong.

components.#.enabled.change: false switches it off at the next gateway start (for PII redaction: payloads are no longer masked).

components.#.config.version.what: The version of this component's config format.
components.#.config.version.change: Another value makes the component refuse its config.

components.#.config.profiles.#.what: One redaction rule: a detector and what to do with what it finds.

components.#.config.profiles.#.builtin.d.what: The built-in detector this rule uses (for example email, phone number, API key).
components.#.config.profiles.#.builtin.d.change: The rule starts matching a different kind of data.

components.#.config.profiles.#.builtin.a.what: What happens to a match (for example replace it).
components.#.config.profiles.#.builtin.a.change: Changes how matches are treated in prompts and responses passing through Relay.

components.#.config.profiles.#.builtin.r.what: The text a match is replaced with.
components.#.config.profiles.#.builtin.r.change: The model and the logs see the new placeholder instead of the matched value.

components.#.config.enable_full_payloads.what: Whether observability events carry full request and response payloads.
components.#.config.enable_full_payloads.change: true puts prompt and answer text into the exported events; the lab keeps it off so content is not exported.

components.#.config.atof.enabled.what: Whether raw ATOF events (Relay's own event log) are written.
components.#.config.atof.enabled.change: false stops the raw event files.

components.#.config.atof.sinks.#.type.change: Events are written to the other sink type.

components.#.config.atof.sinks.#.output_.what: The directory ATOF event files are written to.
components.#.config.atof.sinks.#.output_.change: New events land in the other directory.

components.#.config.atof.sinks.#.filenam.change: New events go to the other file.

components.#.config.atof.sinks.#.mode.what: How the file is written (for example append).
components.#.config.atof.sinks.#.mode.change: Changes whether old events are kept when the gateway restarts.

components.#.config.atif.enabled.what: Whether ATIF trajectories (one file per agent run) are written.

components.#.config.atif.agent_name.what: The agent name recorded in each trajectory.
components.#.config.atif.agent_name.change: New trajectories carry the new name.

components.#.config.atif.output_director.what: The directory trajectory files are written to.
components.#.config.atif.output_director.change: New trajectories land in the other directory.

components.#.config.atif.filename_templa.what: The file name pattern for trajectories.
components.#.config.atif.filename_templa.change: New trajectories are named by the new pattern.

components.#.config.opentelemetry.enable.what: Whether Relay exports OpenTelemetry traces and metrics.
components.#.config.opentelemetry.enable.change: false empties the Relay routing board in Grafana and the Relay traces.

components.#.config.opentelemetry.endpoi.change: Telemetry is sent with the other exporter.

components.#.config.opentelemetry.endpoi.what: The collector address traces are sent to (the metrics address is derived from it).
components.#.config.opentelemetry.endpoi.change: Telemetry goes to the new collector; a wrong address silently drops it.

components.#.config.opentelemetry.endpoi.what: The OTLP transport, for example `http` or `grpc`.
components.#.config.opentelemetry.endpoi.change: It must match what the collector listens for at that address.

components.#.config.opentelemetry.endpoi.what: The service name on Relay's traces; it becomes the Prometheus `job` label of its metrics.
components.#.config.opentelemetry.endpoi.change: Dashboards that filter on the old name stop showing Relay.

components.#.config.opentelemetry.metric.what: Whether metrics are exported as well as traces.
components.#.config.opentelemetry.metric.change: false empties the metric panels of the Relay board.

components.#.config.opentelemetry.metric.what: How often metrics are pushed, in milliseconds.
components.#.config.opentelemetry.metric.change: Lower makes the board fresher at a little more overhead; higher makes it lag.

agents.what: The agents Relay can launch, by name.

agents.*.command.what: The program Relay starts for this agent (for example `claude`).
agents.*.command.change: `nemo-relay` runs the other program for this agent.

version.what: The format version of the presets file; must be 1.
version.change: Any other value makes the whole file invalid.

profiles.*.what: A load preset: one named, repeatable load test you can run from the Actions tab.

profiles.*.description.what: A one-line note shown next to the preset.
profiles.*.description.change: Only the label in the console changes.

profiles.*.model.what: The router alias the load is sent to.
profiles.*.model.change: The next run loads a different engine. Keep loads small on engines other people use.

profiles.*.endpoint_type.what: Which API the synthetic requests use (`chat` by default).
profiles.*.endpoint_type.change: The next run measures the other endpoint.

profiles.*.streaming.what: Whether responses are streamed. Time to first token and inter-token latency need streaming.
profiles.*.streaming.change: false: the run reports only whole-request latency and throughput.

profiles.*.concurrency.what: How many requests are kept in flight at once.
profiles.*.concurrency.change: Higher puts more load on the engine: throughput rises until it saturates, then latency climbs. Other users of the engine feel it.

profiles.*.requests.change: More requests give steadier numbers but the run takes longer.

profiles.*.warmup_requests.what: Requests sent first and not measured, so caches and graphs are warm.
profiles.*.warmup_requests.change: 0 lets cold-start effects into the results.

profiles.*.isl.what: Input sequence length: the mean number of synthetic input tokens per request.
profiles.*.isl.change: Longer inputs weigh on time to first token (prefill).

profiles.*.osl.what: Output sequence length: the mean number of output tokens requested.
profiles.*.osl.change: Longer outputs weigh on decode time and total run time.

profiles.*.timeout_s.what: How long one request may take before it counts as failed, in seconds.
profiles.*.timeout_s.change: Too low turns slow answers into errors; too high lets a stuck engine hold the run.

profiles.*.seed.what: The seed for the synthetic prompts (default 42), so two runs send the same prompts.
profiles.*.seed.change: A different seed sends different prompts, so results are no longer directly comparable with runs made under the old seed.

profiles.what: The named load presets, one block per preset (at most 32).

version.what: The format version of the suites file; must be 1.
version.change: Any other value makes the whole file invalid.

suites.*.what: A benchmark suite: a named set of benchmarks run against one model.

suites.*.description.what: A short note shown with the suite (at most 200 characters).
suites.*.description.change: Only the label in the console changes.

suites.*.model.what: The router alias the suite evaluates.
suites.*.model.change: The next run scores a different model.

suites.*.benchmarks.#.bench.what: Which benchmark to run. Its dataset must have been prefetched (runs are offline).
suites.*.benchmarks.#.bench.change: The next run uses the other benchmark; one that was never prefetched fails.

suites.*.benchmarks.#.max_problems.what: How many problems are sampled (shuffled with a fixed seed, so runs are comparable).
suites.*.benchmarks.#.max_problems.change: More problems give a steadier score but spend more router tokens and time.

suites.*.benchmarks.#.max_tokens.what: The answer length limit per problem.
suites.*.benchmarks.#.max_tokens.change: Too low cuts reasoning answers short and lowers the score; higher costs more tokens.

suites.*.benchmarks.#.repeats.what: How many times each problem is asked (1–8, default 1).
suites.*.benchmarks.#.repeats.change: More repeats average out sampling noise at a multiple of the cost.

suites.*.benchmarks.#.temperature.what: Sampling temperature for the model's answers (0–2; empty = the run's default).
suites.*.benchmarks.#.temperature.change: Higher makes answers more varied and the score noisier from run to run; 0 makes them as repeatable as the engine allows.

suites.what: The named benchmark suites, one block per suite (at most 20).

suites.*.benchmarks.what: The benchmarks the suite runs (at most 8).

version.what: The format version of the recipes file; must be 1.
version.change: Any other value makes the whole file invalid.

recipes.*.what: A compression recipe: what a Model Optimizer job does to which checkpoint.

recipes.*.method.what: What the job does: `reap` (prune MoE experts), `quantize` (lower precision, e.g. NVFP4) or `minitron` (refused here).
recipes.*.method.change: The next job runs a different method and needs that method's keys.

recipes.*.base_model.what: The Hugging Face repo id of the checkpoint to compress, read from the offline cache.
recipes.*.base_model.change: The next job compresses a different model; it must already be in the cache.

recipes.*.output.what: Where the compressed checkpoint is written, under `/runs/`.

recipes.*.description.what: A note shown with the recipe.

recipes.*.preset.what: quantize: the quantization preset, for example `NVFP4`.
recipes.*.preset.change: The output checkpoint uses the other number format (size, speed and accuracy all move).

recipes.*.sparsity.what: reap: the fraction of weights kept, from 0 up to (not including) 1.
recipes.*.sparsity.change: Lower makes a smaller, faster model that loses more accuracy.

recipes.*.config.what: minitron: a config file name in the run directory.
recipes.*.config.change: The job reads the other file.

recipes.what: The named compression recipes, one block per recipe.

models.#.type.what: What this model is used for: `main` is the model being guarded (and, without other entries, the one that runs the self-check prompts).
models.#.type.change: Assigns the model to another role.

models.#.engine.what: How Guardrails talks to the model (`openai` = any OpenAI-compatible API, here the router).
models.#.engine.change: Guardrails uses another client library to reach the model.

models.#.model.what: The model name: a router alias.
models.#.model.change: The guarded answers (and the self checks) come from the other model.

models.#.parameters.what: Parameters passed to the model client.

models.#.parameters.base_url.what: Where the model is reached: the key-injecting router broker on Guardrails' internal network.
models.#.parameters.base_url.change: Another address bypasses the broker; the server has no route anywhere else.

models.#.parameters.temperature.change: Higher makes answers (and self-check verdicts) more varied; lower more repeatable.

models.#.parameters.*.what: A parameter passed to the model client.
models.#.parameters.*.change: The model receives the new value on its next call.

passthrough.what: true = the guarded model answers directly, with no Colang dialog step in between (no embedding model needed).
passthrough.change: false turns on dialog rails, which need flows and an embedding model.

rails.what: The rails: checks run before and after the model.

rails.input.flows.#.what: An input rail: a check run on each user message before the model sees it (for example `self check input`).
rails.input.flows.#.change: Removing one stops that check, so more prompts reach the model; the console refuses a removal unless the file says `# nemo-console: allow-weaken-rails`.

rails.output.flows.#.what: An output rail: a check run on the model's answer before it is returned.
rails.output.flows.#.change: Removing one lets unchecked answers through; the console refuses a removal unless the file says `# nemo-console: allow-weaken-rails`.

rails.output.streaming.enabled.what: Whether output rails check a streamed answer chunk by chunk. A streaming chat needs it when output rails exist.
rails.output.streaming.enabled.change: false: streaming requests with output rails fail.

rails.output.streaming.chunk_size.what: How many tokens are collected before each output-rail check.
rails.output.streaming.chunk_size.change: Smaller checks more often (more judge calls, smoother streaming); larger checks less often (bigger pauses).

rails.output.streaming.context_size.what: Tokens of the previous chunk included with each check, so a phrase split between chunks is still seen.
rails.output.streaming.context_size.change: Larger catches more split content at a little more cost per check.

rails.output.streaming.stream_first.what: false = check each chunk BEFORE it is sent; true = send first and check after.
rails.output.streaming.stream_first.change: true makes streaming faster but can show text a rail later blocks.

instructions.#.content.what: General instructions for the main model.
instructions.#.content.change: The model's behaviour changes on the next request after a restart.

sample_conversation.what: An example conversation given to the model.
sample_conversation.change: Changes the style the model imitates.

prompts.#.what: A prompt template for one rail task.

prompts.#.task.what: Which rail task this template is for (for example `self_check_input`).
prompts.#.task.change: The template is used by the other task; a task with no template falls back to the built-in prompt.

prompts.#.content.what: The prompt the checking model is given. `{{ user_input }}` or `{{ bot_response }}` is replaced by the text being checked; the answer must be Yes (block) or No.
prompts.#.content.change: Changes what gets blocked: a looser prompt lets more through. Test it in the Playground after a restart.

prompts.#.models.#.what: The models this template applies to.
prompts.#.models.#.change: The template is used only with the listed models.

openshell.version.what: The gateway config format version (1 in this build).
openshell.version.change: Another value makes the gateway refuse its config.

openshell.gateway.compute_drivers.#.change: Sandboxes would be started by another driver.

openshell.gateway.host_gateway_ip.what: The IP every sandbox reaches the gateway at (`host.openshell.internal`): the gateway container's static address on the internal network.
openshell.gateway.host_gateway_ip.change: A wrong address leaves sandboxes unable to reach the gateway.

openshell.drivers.docker.network_name.what: The Docker network sandboxes are attached to: an INTERNAL network with no route off the box.
openshell.drivers.docker.network_name.change: A non-internal network would give sandboxes a way out.

openshell.drivers.docker.supervisor_imag.what: The supervisor image injected into every sandbox (it enforces the policy), pinned by digest.
openshell.drivers.docker.supervisor_imag.change: Every new sandbox runs the other supervisor; an unscanned image is a trust change.

openshell.drivers.docker.image_pull_poli.what: Whether images may be pulled at run time. `Never` keeps every image local and pinned.
openshell.drivers.docker.image_pull_poli.change: Allowing pulls would let the Docker daemon download images, which is egress outside the allowlist.

version.change: Another value makes sandbox creation fail.

filesystem_policy.include_workdir.what: Whether the sandbox's work directory is writable.
filesystem_policy.include_workdir.change: false leaves the workload nowhere to write its output.

filesystem_policy.read_only.#.what: A path the workload may read but not write (enforced by Landlock).
filesystem_policy.read_only.#.change: Adding a path exposes it to untrusted dataset scripts; removing one may break the tools that read it.

filesystem_policy.read_write.#.what: A path the workload may write.
filesystem_policy.read_write.#.change: Every writable path is somewhere an untrusted script can leave files.

network_policies.*.what: A named network allowance: which endpoints which programs in the sandbox may reach. Everything else is denied.

network_policies.*.endpoints.#.host.change: Sandboxes may reach the other host instead.

network_policies.*.endpoints.#.port.change: Sandboxes may reach the other port instead.

network_policies.*.endpoints.#.protocol.what: How traffic is inspected (`rest` = HTTP requests matched against the rules).
network_policies.*.endpoints.#.protocol.change: Changes what the supervisor can check.

network_policies.*.endpoints.#.enforceme.what: `enforce` blocks what the rules do not allow; an audit mode only logs.
network_policies.*.endpoints.#.enforceme.change: Anything but enforce lets traffic through.

network_policies.*.endpoints.#.allowed_i.what: The IP range the host may resolve to.
network_policies.*.endpoints.#.allowed_i.change: A wider range lets the name point somewhere else.

network_policies.*.endpoints.#.rules.#.a.what: URL paths allowed (`/v1/**` = the router's API only).
network_policies.*.endpoints.#.rules.#.a.change: Wider paths reach more of the router (for example its admin API).

network_policies.*.binaries.#.path.what: The program allowed to use this endpoint; other programs in the sandbox are refused.
network_policies.*.binaries.#.path.change: Another program gains the network access.

id.what: The provider type id; sandboxes attach a provider of this type.
id.change: Existing providers stop matching the profile.

inference_capable.what: Whether the provider serves model inference.

credentials.#.name.what: The credential's name inside the profile.
credentials.#.name.change: Endpoints and discovery that name it must change too.

credentials.#.env_vars.#.what: The environment variable the credential VALUE is read from when the provider is created. The value is stored by the gateway, never in the sandbox.
credentials.#.env_vars.#.change: The provider must be created again from the new variable.

credentials.#.required.what: Whether a provider can be created without this credential.
credentials.#.required.change: false allows providers with no key.

credentials.#.auth_style.change: The upstream receives the key in another form.

credentials.#.header_name.what: The header the supervisor writes the credential into.
credentials.#.header_name.change: The key goes in another header.

endpoints.#.host.what: A host the credential may be injected for.
endpoints.#.host.change: The key would be sent to another host.

endpoints.#.port.change: The key would be sent to another port.

endpoints.#.path.what: The URL paths the credential is injected on.
endpoints.#.path.change: Wider paths send the key with more requests.

endpoints.#.enforcement.what: `enforce` = only matching requests get the key.

endpoints.#.allowed_ips.#.what: The IP range the host may resolve to.
endpoints.#.allowed_ips.#.change: A wider range lets the name point elsewhere.

endpoints.#.rules.#.allow.method.what: HTTP methods that get the credential.
endpoints.#.rules.#.allow.method.change: Wider sends the key with more requests.

endpoints.#.rules.#.allow.path.what: URL paths that get the credential.
endpoints.#.rules.#.allow.path.change: Wider sends the key with more requests.

binaries.#.what: The program whose requests get the credential.
binaries.#.change: Another program would receive the injected key.

name.what: The Compose project name; container, network and volume names derive from it.
name.change: A new name makes Compose treat it as a different project: the old containers keep running beside new ones.

services.*.image.what: The image the container runs, pinned by tag and digest.
services.*.image.change: The service runs different software on its next recreate; a new image should be scanned first.

services.*.container_name.change: Scripts and health checks that use the old name stop finding it.

services.*.user.what: The user the container runs as.
services.*.user.change: Changes what the process may read and write.

services.*.cap_drop.#.what: A Linux capability removed from the container (`ALL` = every one).
services.*.cap_drop.#.change: Removing an entry gives the container that capability back.

services.*.cap_add.#.what: A Linux capability added to the container.
services.*.cap_add.#.change: Each added capability widens what the container can do.

services.*.security_opt.#.change: Removing it can let processes gain privileges.

services.*.read_only.what: Whether the container's root filesystem is read-only.
services.*.read_only.change: false lets the process modify its own image files.

services.*.restart.change: Changes whether it comes back after a crash or reboot.

services.*.volumes.#.change: Changes what host files the container sees (or can write, without `:ro`).

services.*.environment.what: Environment variables set in the container.

services.*.environment.*.what: An environment variable set in the container.
services.*.environment.*.change: The service reads the new value when it is recreated.

services.*.env_file.#.what: A file environment variables are read from.

services.*.ports.#.change: Opens the service on another host port or address; anything but 127.0.0.1 exposes it to the network.

services.*.command.what: The command the container runs (replaces the image default).
services.*.command.change: The service starts with the new command line.

services.*.command.#.what: One argument of the container's command line.
services.*.command.#.change: The service starts with the changed argument.

services.*.entrypoint.what: The program the container starts (replaces the image default).
services.*.entrypoint.change: The container starts a different program.

services.*.networks.*.ipv4_address.what: The container's fixed IP on this network.
services.*.networks.*.ipv4_address.change: Anything that reaches the service by this IP must change too.

services.*.networks.*.gw_priority.what: Which network provides the default route (highest wins).
services.*.networks.*.gw_priority.change: Moves the container's default route to another network.

services.*.depends_on.#.what: A service started before this one.

services.*.mem_limit.change: Lower can get it killed under load.

services.*.cpus.what: How many CPUs the container may use.
services.*.cpus.change: Changes how fast it can run under load.

services.*.profiles.#.what: A Compose profile: the service starts only when that profile is selected.

networks.*.external.what: true = the network is created outside this file and must already exist.
networks.*.external.change: false makes Compose create (and remove) it itself.

networks.*.internal.what: true = the network has no route off the box.
networks.*.internal.change: false gives everything on it a way out.

networks.*.ipam.config.#.subnet.change: Fixed IPs on it must change too; a range that overlaps another network fails.

volumes.*.what: A named volume the project uses.

services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_C.what: The driver the gateway runs sandboxes with (`docker`).
services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_C.change: Sandboxes would be started another way.

services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_G.what: The address the gateway listens on for the CLI and the sandbox supervisors.
services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_G.change: Clients configured for the old address stop connecting.

services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_D.what: Where the gateway keeps its state database.
services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_D.change: The gateway starts with another (possibly empty) database.

services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_L.what: The directory with the gateway's TLS material.
services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_L.change: The gateway looks for its certificates elsewhere.

services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_T.change: Clients must trust the new certificate.

services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_T.what: The gateway's TLS private key file (a path, not the key).
services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_T.change: The gateway serves with the other key.

services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_T.what: The CA client certificates must be signed by.

services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_E.what: Whether clients must present a certificate (mutual TLS).
services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_E.change: false lets any local client talk to the gateway.

services.gateway.environment.OPENSHELL_T.change: true would try to send usage data (the internal network blocks it anyway).

services.gateway.environment.NEMO_TELEME.what: NeMo telemetry, passed into every sandbox (off).
services.gateway.environment.NEMO_TELEME.change: true would try to send usage data.

services.gateway.environment.HOME.what: The gateway's home directory: the Docker driver resolves the paths it mounts into sandboxes from it.
services.gateway.environment.HOME.change: Sandbox mounts point at other host paths.

services.what: The services whose settings the console overrides. Only `command` and `environment` may be overridden.

services.*.what: A Dynamo service (worker or frontend) whose command line or environment the console manages.

services.*.command.#.what: One argument of the service's command line. The Params tab writes these; only allowlisted flags are accepted and `--model` stays pinned.
services.*.command.#.change: The service starts with the changed argument when it is recreated.

services.*.environment.*.what: An environment variable for the service.
services.*.environment.*.change: The service reads the new value when it is recreated.

services.flare.command.#.what: One argument of `flare run`: the package path, `--offline` (never fetch the publisher from the internet), `--trust-store`, `--gpus` (container-local indices; their count must equal the package's TP size), `--host`, `--port`.
services.flare.command.#.change: Flare starts with the changed argument the next time flare.sh starts it.

services.*.init.what: Whether Docker inserts an init process. false: Flare is PID 1 and handles SIGTERM itself (upstream container doc).
services.*.init.change: true adds an init in front of Flare's own signal handling.

services.*.stop_grace_period.what: How long Docker waits after SIGTERM before killing the container (60 s upstream: graph replay drains before CUDA teardown).
services.*.stop_grace_period.change: Shorter can kill Flare mid-teardown; longer makes a stop slower.

services.*.ulimits.*.what: A resource limit inside the container.

services.*.ulimits.*.soft.what: The soft limit (memlock: bytes of locked memory). Upstream wants unlimited (-1) for pinned transfer buffers; a rootless Docker daemon cannot raise it that far.
services.*.ulimits.*.soft.change: A value above what the daemon allows makes the container fail to start.

services.*.ulimits.*.hard.what: The hard limit (the ceiling the soft limit may rise to).
services.*.ulimits.*.hard.change: It must be at least the soft limit.

services.*.networks.*.aliases.#.what: An extra name other containers on that network reach this one by (`flare` on the ai-lab bus: the router uses flare:8000).
services.*.networks.*.aliases.#.change: Clients that use the old name (the router alias's URL) stop reaching it.

services.*.deploy.resources.reservations.what: The device driver for the GPU reservation (`nvidia`).
services.*.deploy.resources.reservations.change: Another driver gets no NVIDIA GPU.

services.*.deploy.resources.reservations.what: A host GPU index given to the container.
services.*.deploy.resources.reservations.change: The engine runs on other cards; their count must match the package's TP size.

services.*.deploy.resources.reservations.what: What the container may use of the GPU: `compute` (libcuda) and `utility` (nvidia-smi / NVML, used to detect the GPU revision).
services.*.deploy.resources.reservations.change: Without compute Flare cannot load the GPU at all.

paths.what: Where Ignition keeps its inputs and caches inside the preparation container.

paths.hub_cache.what: The Hugging Face cache Ignition reads checkpoints from (the lab's own cache; preparation runs with downloads off).
paths.hub_cache.change: Ignition looks for checkpoints elsewhere; a recipe whose checkpoint is not there fails instead of downloading.

paths.kernel_cache.what: Where tuned kernels are kept between exports.
paths.kernel_cache.change: A new location starts tuning from scratch (slower first export).

paths.package_cache.what: Where Ignition writes prepared package cache entries before they are converted into a package file.
paths.package_cache.change: Exports land elsewhere; `flare.sh convert` must be pointed there.

paths.cuda.what: The CUDA toolkit inside the preparation image (13.2).
paths.cuda.change: A wrong path breaks kernel compilation during export.
